table.title: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية
table.brief: مواقيت الصلاة: المدينة صف عنوان، الأعمدة الفجر الظهر العصر المغرب العشاء بأوقات قصيرة

conditions.browser: Chromium (Playwright build), macOS system fonts, deviceScaleFactor 1

candidates.name: d1r0A
candidates.idea: Keep every city name on one line and give each prayer column its minimum content-fitting width.
candidates.label: gold

whys: City names and prayer times remain whole and easy to scan. The wider city column suits its longer labels, while uniform rows make comparisons straightforward.
All city names and prayer times remain on one line. The wider city column fits the longer names, while consistent row heights make the times easy to scan and compare.
City names and times remain whole on single lines. The wider city column accommodates the longer names, while the compact time columns and uniform rows make comparison easy.

candidates.name: contrast
candidates.idea: Equalizing the columns leaves only 47px of text space for city names, less than the 49px needed for the longest unbreakable unit. It forces a word to break or overflow while giving the time columns more space than they need.
candidates.label: bad

whys: The narrow city column splits مكة المكرمة across three lines, including a break within المكرمة. Uneven row heights interrupt scanning, while the time columns have unused space.

The narrow city column splits مكة المكرمة across three lines, including a break inside المكرمة, and wraps المدينة المنورة. The tall rows interrupt scanning and leave large empty areas in the time columns.

The narrow city column splits مكة المكرمة across three lines, including a break within a word, and wraps المدينة المنورة. The resulting tall rows interrupt scanning, while the time columns have surplus space.

d1.purpose: Provide prayer times for six Saudi cities in a compact reference table.
tasks: Find a city and look across its row for a prayer time.
Compare the same prayer time across cities by scanning a column.
Read the five prayer times in daily order from right to left.
relations: Each time belongs to both its city row and its prayer column.
The five prayer columns form a chronological sequence and have comparable importance.
roles: The rightmost column identifies cities and acts as the entry point for row lookup.
The remaining columns contain times under prayer-name headers.
The header row labels the fields; each body row represents one city.
keep_whole: Each individual word in a city name.
may_wrap: Multiword city names may wrap between words, while remaining clearly associated with their row.
same_scale: The five prayer columns should have a similar visual scale, with enough variation to accommodate their different header widths.
City labels share a role but can occupy a wider column because some names contain multiple words.
d1.h_vs_v: The full city names and minimum widths for all five prayer columns fit exactly within the viewport. Giving more horizontal space to prayer columns requires wrapping some city names and increasing their row heights.

d2.purpose: Present prayer times for six Saudi cities in a compact reference table.
tasks: Find a city and read its five prayer times.
Compare the time of one prayer across cities.
relations: Each city is associated with five times in a fixed prayer sequence.
Each prayer column contains directly comparable times.
roles: The rightmost column names the cities and anchors each row.
The five prayer headers identify the time columns; the remaining rows contain city-specific values.
may_wrap: Multiword city names may wrap between words.
same_scale: The five prayer columns have equivalent roles and should have a broadly similar visual scale, with enough width for their different headers.
d2.h_vs_v: The available width can accommodate every entry on one line if the prayer columns closely follow their minimum content widths. Giving the prayer columns more breathing room requires a narrower city column and taller rows where city names wrap.

d3.purpose: عرض مواقيت الصلوات الخمس في مدن سعودية للمقارنة والرجوع السريع.
tasks: العثور على مدينة وقراءة وقت صلاة محددة
مقارنة أوقات صلاة واحدة بين المدن
relations: كل صف يربط مدينة بمواقيتها الخمسة
ترتيب أعمدة الصلاة يتبع تعاقب الصلوات من الفجر إلى العشاء
roles: العمود الأيمن أسماء المدن وهو مفتاح الصفوف
الأعمدة الخمسة الأخرى مواقيت متكررة ذات وظيفة متساوية
keep_whole: كل كلمة في أسماء المدن ورؤوس الأعمدة
may_wrap: أسماء المدن متعددة الكلمات عند المسافات بينها
same_scale: أعمدة الصلاة الخمسة متقاربة في الوظيفة، مع مراعاة اختلاف عرض رؤوسها
أسماء المدن تشترك في عمود واحد يمكن أن يختلف عرضه عن أعمدة المواقيت
d3.h_vs_v: يمكن احتواء جميع النصوص في سطر واحد عند استغلال العرض المتاح كاملاً؛ وتخصيص مساحة أكبر لأعمدة المواقيت يستلزم التفاف بعض أسماء المدن وزيادة ارتفاع صفوفها.

analysis.strengths: All city names, prayer names, and times remain on one line without clipping or word breaks. The right-to-left sequence is clear, row labels are easy to find, and the consistent row heights support comparison across cities. The table fits the viewport exactly.
analysis.faults: The layout has no spare horizontal space, so it depends on the measured content and font rendering remaining as shown. Within the fixed conditions, there is no evident visual or functional fault.
analysis.spatial_logic: The city column receives enough width for the longest city name. Each prayer-time column receives its measured one-line content width plus padding and borders; together the columns use the full available width.

rounds.insights: The table needs more space for city names than for individual times. Layout P accommodates every entry on one line while preserving a compact, regular grid; shifting width between columns would force at least one column below its measured one-line requirement.

contrast.why: Equalizing the columns leaves only 47px of text space for city names, less than the 49px needed for the longest unbreakable unit. It forces a word to break or overflow while giving the time columns more space than they need.

sameFunctionGroups.why: All five columns contain prayer times and should read as a consistent group. Small width differences accommodate their Arabic headers without wrapping.

synthesis.rationale: P fits the viewport exactly, keeps every city name and time on one line, and preserves the right-to-left reading order. The wider city column accommodates the longer names, while the five time columns remain close enough in width to support comparison.

general: Protect complete words and values before optimizing compactness.
Size columns according to their content and reading function; related columns should have a visually coherent scale.
specific: The city column needs 112px to hold its widest name on one line with the fixed padding and border.
The prayer-time columns can fit their headers and values in 56–68px each.

synthesis.tradeoffs: P uses the full 414px viewport, leaving no horizontal spare space, but achieves a compact table with no wrapping or scrolling.
synthesis.uncertain: Only P was presented as a candidate, so no comparison with other rendered layouts is possible.

critique.good: All city names, prayer headers, and times stay on one line. Uniform row heights support quick scanning across rows and down columns, and the table fits the viewport exactly.
critique.problems: The city column is noticeably wider than the prayer columns, while the prayer columns are tight around their headers. The difference is functional, though: it preserves complete city names and a compact, regular grid.
critique.cause: The 112 px city column accommodates the longest full name; the prayer columns use their minimum content widths of 56, 56, 59, 68, and 62 px.

critique.good: All headers and times remain whole, and the prayer columns have a little more breathing room. The wrapped city names remain clearly associated with their rows.
critique.problems: Two city names wrap, making their rows substantially taller and interrupting the otherwise regular scanning rhythm. The extra space in the prayer columns provides limited benefit for the short times.
critique.cause: Reducing the city column to 91 px forces مكة المكرمة and المدينة المنورة onto two lines; the recovered width is distributed across the prayer columns.

critique.good: Headers and times remain whole, and the prayer columns have generous space. Individual words in city names are preserved.
critique.problems: The narrow city column makes the entry point feel compressed, while the prayer columns have more space than their short contents need. Two tall rows disrupt the table’s rhythm without improving lookup.
critique.cause: The 70 px city column is only wide enough for the longest individual city-name word, while the prayer columns expand to 64, 64, 67, 78, and 70 px.

critique.good: All headers and times remain whole and legible, and the five prayer columns have a comparable visual scale. The table fits the viewport.
critique.problems: المدينة المنورة wraps onto two lines, making its row taller than the others and interrupting the otherwise even rhythm of the table.
critique.cause: The 100px city column is too narrow for the full name; the additional width given to the prayer columns comes at the cost of that wrap.

critique.good: Every city name, header and time fits on one line. Even row heights support scanning across cities and down prayer columns, and the table fits the viewport exactly.
critique.problems: The prayer columns are compact, with little spare horizontal space around the widest headers, but the rendered labels remain legible and distinct.
critique.cause: The 112px city column uses the width needed to keep the longest name whole, leaving the prayer columns at their minimum content widths.

critique.good: All city names, prayer headers and times stay on one line. Uniform row heights make the table compact and support quick comparison down each prayer column.
critique.problems: The first two prayer columns look tight, while the city column occupies a noticeably larger share of the table. The tight spacing is most apparent around the prayer headers.
critique.cause: The 112px city column uses the full width needed for the longest city name, leaving the first two prayer columns at their 56px minimum and العصر at 59px.

critique.good: The prayer columns have more breathing room, and the headers and times remain intact. The city names wrap between words and remain readable.
critique.problems: Two taller rows interrupt the otherwise even rhythm and spread the times farther apart for column comparison. The extra width given to prayer columns costs substantial vertical space.
critique.cause: The 80px city column wraps both multiword city names; the reclaimed width is distributed across the five prayer columns.

critique.good: The prayer columns have a consistent visual scale, and all prayer headers and times remain whole. The wrapped city names are still readable.
critique.problems: The two tall rows interrupt the table's rhythm, while the city column feels compressed relative to the nearly equal prayer columns. The equal widths give some short headers more space than they need.
critique.cause: The city column is reduced to its 70px minimum, wrapping both multiword names, while prayer columns are set to 68–69px despite their different content widths.

critique.good: All headers and time values remain whole and visible. The prayer columns have a broadly consistent scale, and the table fits the viewport.
critique.problems: Two city names wrap onto two lines, making those rows taller and interrupting the otherwise even rhythm. This also makes the table longer for both row lookup and column comparison.
critique.cause: The 96px city column is too narrow for the two longest names; the extra width is distributed among the prayer columns.

critique.good: Every city, header and time fits on one line. Equal row heights support quick comparison down each prayer column, while the rightmost city column provides a clear row anchor. The table fits exactly within the viewport.
critique.problems: The prayer columns are compact, especially around the longer headers, but the rendered text remains readable and distinct.
critique.cause: The 112px city column uses the space needed to keep every name whole, leaving the prayer columns close to their content-width requirements.

critique.good: All city names, prayer headers and times remain on one line. Uniform row heights support quick scanning and comparison, and the table fits the viewport.
critique.problems: The prayer columns are compact, especially around the wider headers, so the horizontal spacing is somewhat tight.
critique.cause: The 112px city column accommodates the longest city name on one line, leaving the prayer columns at their measured minimum widths.

critique.good: The prayer columns have more breathing room, and city names wrap only at word boundaries. All headers and times remain whole.
critique.problems: Two taller rows interrupt the otherwise regular rhythm and make it slightly slower to scan across cities.
critique.cause: The 80px city column cannot hold the two longest city names on one line; the recovered width is distributed across the prayer columns.

critique.good: All text remains visible, and the wrapped city names break at spaces. The wider المغرب and العشاء columns give their headers ample room.
critique.problems: The prayer columns feel uneven: the two leftmost columns contain conspicuous empty space while the other three remain tight. The two taller city rows also interrupt the scanning rhythm.
critique.cause: The 70px city column forces two names to wrap, while the 90px and 82px prayer columns receive much more width than the 56–59px columns.

critique.good: All headers and times remain intact, and the prayer columns have comfortable, broadly consistent widths. The table fits the viewport.
critique.problems: Two city names wrap, making their rows taller and interrupting the otherwise regular rhythm. The extra height also makes comparison down the prayer columns less compact.
critique.cause: The 96px city column is too narrow for the two longest names on one line; the prayer columns take the space needed to keep them whole.

critique.good: Every city name, header and time fits on one line. Uniform row heights support scanning across cities and down prayer columns, and the complete table fits the viewport.
critique.problems: The prayer columns are compact, particularly around their longer headers, but the text remains visible and the fixed padding is preserved.
critique.cause: The 112px city column accommodates the longest name, while the prayer columns use their available minimum widths. At this viewport, widening one would require narrowing another column.

d2r0A.idea: Keep every city on one line and size each prayer column to its content, producing a compact table with varied prayer-column widths.

d2r0B.idea: Allow longer city names to wrap and give all five prayer columns additional space while retaining widths proportional to their headers.

d2r0C.idea: Use a narrow city column and five nearly equal prayer columns to emphasize comparison down the time columns, accepting more wrapping in city names.

d1r0A.idea: Keep every city name on one line and give each prayer column its minimum content-fitting width.

d1r0B.idea: Allow longer city names to wrap while distributing the released space across the prayer columns for a more open comparison area.

d1r0C.idea: Use a compact city-label column that wraps multiword names and devote the remaining width to spacious prayer-time columns.

d3r0A.idea: إبقاء أسماء المدن والمواقيت كلها في سطر واحد مع منح كل عمود صلاة الحد اللازم لمحتواه.

d3r0B.idea: السماح بالتفاف أسماء المدن الطويلة لتوزيع مساحة إضافية متقاربة على أعمدة الصلاة الخمسة.

d3r0C.idea: ضغط عمود المدن إلى عرض أطول كلمة وتخصيص المساحة المحررة لعمودي المغرب والعشاء مع إبقاء بقية أعمدة الصلاة عند حدها اللازم.

d2r1A.idea: Test an intermediate city width that may keep the shorter multiword name on one line while giving every prayer column more room than in A. The unequal prayer widths reflect their different header lengths; the render will show whether the remaining wrap and spacing improve the balance.

d1r1A.idea: Test an intermediate city width with modestly wider prayer columns. This may allow one multiword city name to remain on one line while giving the prayer headers more room; the render will show whether the resulting row-height variation is worthwhile.

d3r1A.idea: Test a middle ground: give the prayer columns modestly more room than in A while keeping the city column wider than in B. The longest city name will wrap, so the render can show whether the extra space around the prayer headers justifies the change in row rhythm.

L03.why: The noon header breaks inside the word, and several noon times split across lines. Tall rows make comparison difficult.

L02.why: The sunset and night prayer headers break inside words, leaving isolated letters on a second line. Times and city names remain easy to scan.

L04.why: Both two-word city names wrap naturally, while all prayer labels and times stay intact. The two taller rows interrupt the otherwise regular scan.

L07.why: The dawn header and two dawn times break inside their content, producing isolated characters and uneven rows.

L06.why: The longer city name wraps naturally, with intact headers and times. Its single taller row and column proportions are very close in effect to G.

L08.why: The الفجر heading and two times split across lines. Lookup suffers where digits fall onto a second line, and the tall rows interrupt the table’s rhythm.

L13.why: The body reads cleanly, but المغرب splits off its final letter. The tall header and extra width in the neighboring column make the allocation feel uneven.
